Maria Lopez: Quick heads-up — FP8 kernel swap on t4-east shows a perf regression vs INT8 baseline. KV cache miss rate jumped and 95th tail latency spiked.
Ashwin Patel: ugh. numbers?
Maria Lopez: Paste from perf-run (short):
```
model: redwood-ggml-mix-v2
hw: t4.x8
baseline (INT8): p95=72ms, p99=180ms, kv_miss=2.1%
fp8-kernel-v3: p95=110ms, p99=420ms, kv_miss=9.8%
cpu/gpu util similar; batching unchanged
```
Maria Lopez: KV miss looks correlated with longer KV warmup for mixed-precision kernel path :thinking:
Kai Zhou: Did the kernel switch change KV cache layout or prefetch stride? We changed kernel tile size in v3, might interact with kv offset calculations.
Ashwin Patel: I profiled memory access — v3 reads kv pages in 256B strides vs 1KB previously. More random I/O for common seqlen distribution.
Jen Miller: Also saw a bump in prefix cache invalidations in logs for high-concurrency routes.
Maria Lopez: I'm leaning toward calibration dataset causing different activation distributions -> different kv cache footprints + quant rounding -> slightly different token lengths into the model and hence cache churn.
Kai Zhou: Hmm. Are we sure it's dataset vs kernel? Could be batching heuristic: v3 opportunistic batching increased micro-batch sizes on tail, increasing seqlens that trigger different KV path.
Ashwin Patel: Good point. I ran an A/B: same kernel, toggled batching heuristic -> p95 moves ~15-20ms. With fp8-kernel + old batching it still worse than INT8 but p95 ~95ms, not 110.
Maria Lopez: Interesting. So it's multiplicative: kernel stride change + batching shift + calibration sample outliers.
profiler-bot: Automated note: calibration-run-2048749000 completed. sample_count=1024, pct_long_seq(>1024)=0.9%, pct_outliers=1.8%
Ashwin Patel: Calibration samples show a tiny long-tail. If we remove top 0.5% seqlen outliers and run per-channel calibration, FP8 quant params tighten and avg absolute quant error drops.
Jen Miller: Can we try per-channel instead of per-tensor? Per-channel tends to reduce range overestimation for weights with skew.
Kai Zhou: Yes but per-channel increases kernel complexity and memory for scales. For our t4 kernels it's fine, overhead ~1-2% memory, but throughput might change.
Maria Lopez: Proposal: run a 3-way micro-experiment across same hardware: (A) FP8-kernel-v3 + old batching + per-channel calibration with outlier trim(0.5%) (B) FP8-kernel-v3 + old batching + per-tensor calibration with same trim (C) INT8 baseline. Collect p95/p99, kv_miss, prefix invalidations, and quant_error on calibration set.
Ashwin Patel: I'll own the A/B/C runs. Plan: 10k requests distributed across seqlen histogram, reproduce traffic envelope. Expected runtime ~2h.
Kai Zhou: I'll add a microprofiling hook to dump kv access stride heatmaps and batching micro-batch size distribution to S3 so we can correlate.
Jen Miller: I'll update the calibration pipeline to support trim-percent param and emit per-channel stats. Small PR incoming.
Maria Lopez: Great. If A looks close to INT8 we can keep v3 but enable per-channel by default and add outlier-trim in calibration tool.
Ashwin Patel: If not, fallback is to revert tile size change or patch kernel to read 1KB strides with prefetch aggregation.
Maria Lopez: Notes for the thread: avoid large sample sets with long-tail dialogs during calibration; prefer stratified sampler across seqlen buckets. Also add a small synthetic tail to ensure kv-warmup exercised.
Kai Zhou: ack. I'll produce heatmaps and upload to eng-ml/snapshots/2048754321/ by EOD.
profiler-bot: CI note: perf-run-2048754321 started by @AshwinPatel at 2048754330
Maria Lopez: thanks — will check results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Ashwin Patel: assigning myself and tagging Jen/Kai in the experiment doc. Will post run links here when done.
